bel_sandwich_cook.text: What'll it be? We do the lot. If you want it Ulster-style, you want a fry.
An Ulster fry has sausage, bacon, egg, potato bread and a soda farl. A farl is a triangle of bread raised with baking soda, not yeast.

then.text: That is all I have, I am afraid. Off you go, and mind how you go.

else.text: Take one for the road. Wee bit of crumb never hurt anybody.

belfast_quizmaster.text: Right, quiz night at the Sandwich Bar. A toastie for every right answer, which is a lie, but it keeps you listening.
Five questions. Phones away. Wee Dave, I can see you down there, and the answer is not on your leg.
Fancy a round? Five questions, no phones.

else.text: Fair dos. Come back when you're feeling brave.

then.text: Daily number: £6.40. I've stuck it on the fridge. The lunch deal and I are taking some time apart.

else.text: Don't look at my receipts. I have £140 a week. My share of rent is £70, and phone and bus pass come to £25.
I've bought a £4.50 lunch deal every day since September, and I'm baffled about why I'm broke by Thursday.
What can she spend a day on everything else?

then.text: I wish. £140 less £70 less £25 leaves £45, and that has to last seven days.
Yes. £45 over seven days is about £6.40 a day, and the lunch deal is already most of it. Oh no.
Not quite. £140 less £70 less £25 leaves £45 for the week. Divided by seven, it's far less than that.

else.text: So the method is: write down what comes in, take off what you can't dodge, divide the rest by seven, and that's your daily number.
And put a little aside for the month the boiler goes. Even £5 a week is £260 a year. Future me will be thrilled.
Here, a farl. Homemade lunch is about a quarter of the price and half as sad.
Noted in the Almanac under Things worth knowing.
